nodes.label: Kanbots (upstream project)
nodes.author: Leonardo Cunha
nodes.rationale: Upstream of the Kodra fork; the published npx `kanbots` package and packaged binaries are the upstream distribution, not Kodra. Package scope @kanbots/* is a preserved compatibility identifier.

nodes.label: Electron process model (no HTTP for renderer)
nodes.norm_label: electron process model (no http for renderer)
nodes.rationale: Every renderer-to-main call goes over Electron IPC; the only HTTP surface is the local tool bridge, which exists solely so the out-of-process MCP server can reach in-Electron handlers.

nodes.label: Tool bridge security model
nodes.rationale: Bridge binds 127.0.0.1 only and rotates a bearer token per Electron session; the token authorizes everything so it must be treated as a session secret.

nodes.label: CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs on every PR and push to main; the release workflow deliberately does not run these checks, so CI is the only gate stopping a broken commit from landing. Concurrency group per ref with cancel-in-progress to avoid redundant runs.

nodes.label: CI verify job (build, typecheck, lint, format, test)
nodes.norm_label: ci verify job (build, typecheck, lint, format, test)
nodes.rationale: Build runs BEFORE typecheck and tests because workspace packages resolve each other through dist/ (types and runtime). pnpm is enabled via corepack and pinned by the packageManager field; install uses --frozen-lockfile.

nodes.label: Release build matrix job (mac/win/linux)
nodes.rationale: Runs after bump and prepare-release; on the dispatch path builds the new tag, on the manual tag-push path builds github.ref directly. fail-fast is false so one OS failing does not cancel the others; packaging output is uploaded as an artifact on failure for debugging.

nodes.label: Release bump job (version bump, commit, tag)
nodes.norm_label: release bump job (version bump, commit, tag)
nodes.rationale: Uses npm version --no-git-tag-version plus explicit git add/commit/tag in packages/desktop because npm version's built-in git flow is unreliable in a workspace + detached checkout (exits 0 while creating neither commit nor tag). checkout@v4 leaves HEAD detached, so HEAD and the tag are pushed explicitly.

nodes.label: Prepare-release job (create GitHub release once)
nodes.rationale: GitHub allows multiple releases per tag; when matrix jobs publish concurrently two electron-builder publishers can race release creation and strand assets on different release objects for the same tag (happened on v1.2.0 and v1.2.2). The release is therefore created exactly once BEFORE the matrix starts so builders only ever attach assets.

nodes.label: Release Workflow
nodes.rationale: Kept as ONE workflow (dispatch cuts version + tag, then build matrix runs off the tag; manual v* tag pushes also build) because tag pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger other workflows (GitHub anti-recursion rule), so a separate tag-triggered build workflow would never fire for CI-cut releases. Concurrency cancel-in-progress is false so releases are never aborted mid-way.

nodes.label: pnpm workspace (packages/*)
nodes.rationale: Monorepo layout: every directory under packages/ is a workspace package; CI and release rely on pnpm --filter to target @kanbots/desktop.

nodes.label: electron-builder publish
nodes.rationale: Invoked per-OS via pnpm --filter @kanbots/desktop exec electron-builder <targets> --publish always, attaching assets to the pre-created GitHub release.

nodes.label: Auto-update of packaged builds
nodes.rationale: Packaged installs self-update from GitHub releases cut by the tag-driven pipeline.

nodes.label: Tag-driven multi-OS release pipeline (as described in README)
nodes.norm_label: tag-driven multi-os release pipeline (as described in readme)
nodes.rationale: README describes two workflows (`release-cut` bumps + tags, `release-build` builds mac/linux/win); the actual .github/workflows/release.yml is a single merged workflow. Documentation drift flagged AMBIGUOUS. States the first Kodra release has not been cut yet.

nodes.label: @kanbots/desktop package (Electron shell)
nodes.rationale: Electron shell, IPC bridge, workspace picker; the package whose version is bumped and packaged by the release workflow.

nodes.label: WSL hardware acceleration disable (KODRA_FORCE_GPU)
nodes.rationale: Under WSL hardware acceleration is disabled automatically to avoid GPU compositing artifacts; KODRA_FORCE_GPU=1 overrides.

nodes.label: rtk.assumeInstalled config hint
nodes.rationale: A hint, not a measurement: Kodra annotates the cost-budget UI with projected savings but cannot measure RTK's effect.

nodes.label: RTK (Rust Token Killer)
nodes.rationale: Opt-in, user-installed CLI that compresses command output so agents spend fewer tokens; Kodra neither bundles nor invokes it. It is the cost-optimization axis, orthogonal to agentmemory.

nodes.label: ADR-0001 Integration vision: memory and cost optimization
nodes.norm_label: adr-0001 integration vision: memory and cost optimization

nodes.label: Autopilot qa mode
nodes.rationale: Autonomous fix loop: run AutopilotCheckCommands in the worktree, dispatch a fix run on a derived child issue per failure, repeat until green or budget exhausted.

nodes.label: kodra-decision fenced block protocol
nodes.rationale: Decision cards are detected by regex over assistant text, so they work for any CLI steered by system prompt to emit the fence; risk is silent degradation if a CLI reformats fenced code.

nodes.label: Migrated Kodra-native names (.kodra/, kodra/issue-* branches, kodra-decision)
nodes.norm_label: migrated kodra-native names (.kodra/, kodra/issue-* branches, kodra-decision)
nodes.rationale: New workspaces and worktrees use .kodra/ with legacy-first resolution (describeKanbotsDir) so existing .kanbots/ workspaces keep working; hardcoding .kanbots/ previously hijacked fresh .kodra/ workspaces on attachment upload.

nodes.label: bypassPermissions hands-off mode
nodes.rationale: Runs are hands-off because the agent may use any tool without per-call prompts; safety is delegated to containment and the worktree pre-push hook instead of tool prompts.

nodes.label: Containment mode (off/warn/pause)
nodes.rationale: Because any CLI can edit paths outside the worktree, every tool_use target path is compared to the worktree root; the mode decides whether escapes are ignored, logged, or pause the run for a decision.

nodes.label: Worktree pre-push hook
nodes.rationale: A pre-push hook that always exits non-zero guarantees the agent can never publish, even under bypassPermissions; promotion is the only path by which agent commits reach real branches.

nodes.label: Promotion (promote commit / draft PR / discard)
nodes.rationale: Promotion is the sole channel by which agent work lands on user branches, keeping the human as the explicit gate.

nodes.label: Worktree lifecycle
nodes.rationale: One isolated git worktree per run (.kanbots/worktrees/issue-<n>-<runId>, branch kanbots/issue-<n>-<runId>) with an identity file for orphan recovery; worktrees persist after the run so many parked runs can coexist across issues.

nodes.label: Codex open questions and risks
nodes.rationale: Flags, event schema, session/resume, approval model, tool naming for containment, and cost reporting must be confirmed against the real binary before Phase 2 because guesses compound into rewrites.

nodes.label: Codex rollout phasing
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 extracts the claude adapter with no behavior change (the one risky refactor, reviewed alone); Phase 2 adds codex-cli behind a hidden flag; Phase 3 exposes UI and docs.

nodes.label: GitHub issue mode
nodes.rationale: Kanban status and agent state are encoded as status:* and agent:* labels so GitHub itself stays the source of truth; failed auth leaves the app read-only rather than failing writes silently.

nodes.label: ProviderId catalogue (agent vs chat-only)
nodes.rationale: Issue drafting and Sentry analysis stay on Claude even when Codex is default because those short-form prompts rely on Claude's output format.

nodes.label: codex-cli provider id
nodes.rationale: A separate 'codex-cli' id rather than reusing 'openai': the chat provider is a raw API transport while Codex is a local CLI with different credentials and error modes; mirrors the existing 'claude-code' vs 'anthropic' split.

nodes.label: Provider key storage (safeStorage encryption)
nodes.rationale: Keys live in the providers table encrypted via Electron safeStorage with a recorded keyEncryption flag; they never leave the workspace folder.

nodes.label: Three independent auth layers (Cloud, GitHub, agent CLIs)
nodes.norm_label: three independent auth layers (cloud, github, agent clis)
nodes.rationale: Each layer is checked in isolation; being signed in to one does not affect the others, which is the most common source of confusion.

nodes.label: Kodra as rebranded fork of Kanbots
nodes.norm_label: kodra as rebranded fork of kanbots

nodes.label: Rebranding migration debt
nodes.rationale: Stale screenshots, upstream-owned npm package, no Kodra domain, and the fork repo still named kanbots remain open TODOs.

nodes.label: Startup environment variables (KANBOTS_*)
nodes.rationale: Legacy provider-key env vars are consulted only on first run for one-time import into the providers table, never at runtime.

nodes.label: MCP tool set (issue CRUD + agent runs)
nodes.norm_label: mcp tool set (issue crud + agent runs)

nodes.label: Kodra Cloud (app.kanbots.dev remote workspaces)
nodes.rationale: Cloud sign-in is optional and adds a parallel axis of remote workspaces (orgs, projects, cards, runs, costs) without unlocking or altering the local-first core.

nodes.label: RTK PreToolUse hook
nodes.rationale: Hook lives in the user's agent CLI config, so Kodra-spawned runs inherit it with no per-worktree setup; an explicit --mcp-config/settings override may bypass it.

nodes.label: Autopilot feature-dev mode
nodes.rationale: Self-evolving parallel mode: up to 4 slots each claim the next persona round-robin (cycle_index), personas split issues into child cards via splitIssue, so the backlog grows and shrinks under the orchestrator without user intervention.

nodes.label: Retained kanbots compatibility identifiers
nodes.rationale: Package scope, .kanbots/ data dirs, KANBOTS_* env vars, kanbots:* IPC channels, and the Electron userData name are kept because they are published interfaces or on-disk data; renaming needs a coordinated migration. Treated as compatibility debt, not branding.

nodes.label: Agent memory (workspace-scoped MCP memory server)
nodes.rationale: Spawned agents can carry a persistent workspace-scoped memory server over MCP so context survives across runs; recall is configured in Memory settings.

nodes.label: Agent run lifecycle (dispatch -> worktree -> stream -> decision -> post-run actions)
nodes.norm_label: agent run lifecycle (dispatch -> worktree -> stream -> decision -> post-run actions)
nodes.rationale: Dispatch creates .kodra/worktrees/issue-<n>-<runId>/ branched from the default branch, spawns claude -p or codex exec with stream-JSON output, parses every event and forwards to the UI; decision requests pause the run until answered. After the run the worktree stays on disk for preview, promote, draft PR, fork run, or discard.

nodes.label: Fork run into existing worktree
nodes.rationale: A follow-up run can be dispatched into an existing worktree to iterate on its state rather than starting from a fresh branch.

nodes.label: kodra-mcp-server (board over MCP)
nodes.rationale: Exposes the board over Model Context Protocol so Cursor, Claude Desktop, or any MCP-aware client can drive it; kanbots-mcp-server remains as a legacy alias.

nodes.label: Promote worktree (commit or draft PR)
nodes.rationale: Lands an agent's worktree as a real commit on the user's branch, or opens a draft PR in GitHub mode; uses .kodra/promote/ as staging area.

nodes.label: Session resume (agent session id + terminal command)
nodes.norm_label: session resume (agent session id + terminal command)

nodes.label: .kodra/ workspace data directory
nodes.rationale: New workspaces use .kodra/; existing ones keep .kanbots/ for backward compatibility. Contains db.sqlite, config.json, worktrees/, attachments/, mcp-runtime/, specs/, promote/. Nothing is written outside this directory or the worktrees it creates.

nodes.label: @kanbots/dispatcher package
nodes.rationale: Agent runtime: spawns the configured agent CLI, parses its stream output, manages worktrees.

nodes.label: Per-run worktree isolation with pre-push hook
nodes.norm_label: per-run worktree isolation with pre-push hook
nodes.rationale: Each run gets its own git worktree so parallel agents cannot clobber each other; a pre-push hook installed in every worktree prevents agents from pushing to remote on their own. Promotion is always an explicit user step (containment).

nodes.label: Web app HTML entry (Vite index.html)
nodes.rationale: Minimal Vite shell: #root mount node, dark theme-color #0A0C10, SVG favicon /kodra-mark.svg, loads /src/main.tsx as an ES module.

nodes.label: Launcher (bin/kanbots.js)
nodes.rationale: Locates the vendored binary, spawns it with inherited stdio, and forwards SIGINT/SIGTERM so Ctrl+C works cleanly.

nodes.label: postinstall script (scripts/postinstall.js)
nodes.rationale: Detects platform, downloads the matching release asset, unpacks into vendor/<platform>/, and clears the macOS quarantine attribute. Can be skipped with KANBOTS_SKIP_POSTINSTALL=1 for CI; the launcher re-runs it once on demand if npx cache paths or --ignore-scripts skipped it.

nodes.label: Kanbots npx launcher (npx kanbots)
nodes.rationale: One-command installer that ships the upstream Kanbots distribution (Kodra fork builds from source). Downloads the ~80MB platform binary from GitHub releases on first run and caches it; later runs launch directly. The npx-cli/package.json version IS the release version the postinstall looks for, so it must match the release tag exactly.

nodes.label: Kodra (agentic development workspace)
nodes.rationale: A kanban board that runs 12 agent CLIs in parallel, each run isolated in its own worktree. Fork of Kanbots by Leonardo Cunha, rebranded; MIT license and attribution retained.

nodes.label: macOS Gatekeeper quarantine clearing (xattr -rd)
nodes.rationale: macOS builds are unsigned so Gatekeeper quarantines them; postinstall clears com.apple.quarantine automatically, the same step install-mac.sh performs.

nodes.label: Windows manual install gap
nodes.rationale: Automated Windows install is not wired up; npx kanbots on Windows prints a link to the NSIS installer instead.

nodes.label: Unsigned packaged builds (Gatekeeper / SmartScreen)
nodes.rationale: Builds are unsigned, so macOS Gatekeeper rejects the dmg and Windows SmartScreen warns; a one-line install script clears the quarantine flag (xattr -d com.apple.quarantine) as a workaround.

nodes.label: Custom Persona Creation (New Persona, Stored Locally)
nodes.norm_label: custom persona creation (new persona, stored locally)

nodes.label: Agent Client Protocol (ACP) over stdio
nodes.rationale: Generic adapter path: any binary speaking ACP over stdio can be dispatched, extending beyond the 11 named CLIs.

nodes.label: Autopilot (dispatch loop)
nodes.rationale: Turns dispatch from a one-shot click into a loop. Both modes write to the autopilot_sessions table so cycle history and child runs are visible and the whole tree can be stopped from one button.

nodes.label: feature-dev autopilot mode
nodes.rationale: Multi-persona, up to 4 parallel slots, round-robin through the persona roster; agents split into subtasks. Ideation runs through the session's own provider CLI (not just claude). Stops on completion, stop button, or session cost budget, and fails fast with a root-cause reason after 5 consecutive failed ideate/dispatch iterations instead of retrying forever.

nodes.label: qa autopilot mode
nodes.rationale: Runs configurable check commands (typecheck/tests/lint/build/e2e), optionally starts and watches a dev server, and dispatches fix runs against whatever fails.

nodes.label: Subscription / plan usage awareness
nodes.rationale: Plan usage for Claude, Codex, Antigravity and Copilot is surfaced so work can be spread across plans the user already pays for.

nodes.label: Supported agent CLIs (12 providers)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Antigravity, Cursor, Copilot, Amp, OpenCode, Droid, CCR, Qwen, plus any ACP-compatible CLI. Each CLI reuses its own auth: the user never signs into Kodra, Kodra calls the CLI already on PATH.

nodes.rationale: Pure handler library + agent supervisor, deliberately with no HTTP server (invoked over the Electron IPC bridge).

nodes.rationale: CLI adapters and provider catalogue.

nodes.label: SIL Open Font License 1.1
nodes.rationale: All bundled web fonts (Inter Tight, Noto Sans Math/Symbols/Symbols 2, Noto Color Emoji) are redistributed under OFL 1.1, which permits bundling in the app as long as the license text ships with the fonts — hence one OFL-*.txt per font family in src/assets/fonts.

nodes.label: Build and packaging pipeline
nodes.rationale: Cross-host packaging unsupported because ensure:native fetches the better-sqlite3 prebuild for the host platform/arch.

nodes.label: Auto-update via electron-updater
nodes.rationale: macOS can only detect updates while unsigned (Squirrel.Mac needs a signed bundle); private repo breaks the unauthenticated GitHub feed until public or a KODRA_UPDATE_FEED_URL mirror exists.

nodes.label: Stable artifact naming scheme
nodes.rationale: Predictable kodra-<version>-<platform> names let the marketing site hardcode releases/latest/download links.

nodes.label: release.yml single-workflow release pipeline
nodes.rationale: One workflow cuts the version and builds on three OSes because tag pushes made with the runner GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger other workflows; releases are published immediately since electron-updater ignores drafts.

nodes.label: Unsigned builds (Gatekeeper / SmartScreen)
nodes.rationale: Code-signing certificates are paid and deferred until revenue covers them; users bypass Gatekeeper via xattr and SmartScreen via Run anyway.

nodes.label: IssueSource contract
nodes.rationale: Abstraction over the issue backend so the board works identically against SQLite (LocalIssueSource) or GitHub.

nodes.label: Workspace modes (local vs github)
nodes.rationale: local mode stores issues in SQLite for solo work; github mode drives real issues via GitHub REST/Octokit, mirroring column moves as status:* label edits.

nodes.label: @kanbots/core package
nodes.rationale: Domain types, GitHub client, IssueSource contract.

nodes.label: @kanbots/local-store package
nodes.rationale: SQLite schema, migrations, repos, LocalIssueSource.

nodes.label: ADR status lifecycle (Proposed -> Accepted -> Deprecated | Superseded)
nodes.norm_label: adr status lifecycle (proposed -> accepted -> deprecated | superseded)
nodes.rationale: Status changes are real commits, not silent edits, so the decision log doubles as history.

nodes.label: agentmemory (rohitg00/agentmemory) persistent memory server
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the fork's memory layer instead of building in-house: already provides hybrid search (BM25 + all-MiniLM-L6-v2 vectors + knowledge graph), 54 MCP tools, 12 lifecycle hooks, team namespaces, SQLite via iii engine, no cloud/LLM key required. Local daemon on :3111 REST, :3112 stream, :3113 web viewer, :49134 iii-engine WebSocket.

nodes.label: Per-run/per-session USD cost budgets (runCostBudgetUsd, sessionCostBudgetUsd)
nodes.rationale: kanbots already stops runs that breach the cap; command-output tokens are a meaningful slice of that cost, which is what makes rtk relevant and why recall injection must be cost-aware.

nodes.label: Stateless per-issue agent runs in isolated worktrees
nodes.norm_label: stateless per-issue agent runs in isolated worktrees
nodes.rationale: Nothing an agent learned carries to the next run on the same module — the core problem the memory axis addresses.

nodes.label: agentmemory health detection on startup
nodes.rationale: Pings http://localhost:3111/agentmemory/health on launch and when the memory panel opens; surfaces running/not-running in the UI so failure is never silent.

nodes.label: iii-engine (pinned v0.11.2, WebSocket :49134)
nodes.rationale: Auto-downloaded by agentmemory to ~/.agentmemory/bin/; refuses to attach if another iii engine is bound to :49134 — the root of the port-conflict concern.

nodes.label: Settings toggle: start agentmemory with kanbots (default off)
nodes.norm_label: settings toggle: start agentmemory with kanbots (default off)

nodes.label: Version pin awareness (record agentmemory + iii-engine versions)
nodes.norm_label: version pin awareness (record agentmemory + iii-engine versions)
nodes.rationale: Recorded in .kanbots/db.sqlite; known-bad versions warn in the UI but do not block.

nodes.label: @agentmemory/mcp stdio shim
nodes.rationale: stdio MCP shim spawned via `npx -y @agentmemory/mcp`; proxies to REST at AGENTMEMORY_URL (localhost:3111). Exposes memory_* tools, disjoint from the tool-bridge namespace.

nodes.label: kanbots tool-bridge MCP server (packages/api/src/tool-bridge.ts)
nodes.rationale: Local HTTP service bound to 127.0.0.1 on a random port, token-gated; lets agents drive the board back (listIssues, dispatchAgent). Precedent for managed local services and for MCP injection.

nodes.label: .kanbots/config.json `memory` section (enabled/provider/url/secret/scope)
nodes.rationale: enabled:false or omission means no memory wiring — fully backward-compatible with upstream kanbots. Validated by packages/local-store/src/workspace.ts like containmentMode/checks.

nodes.label: Transient per-run MCP config (.kanbots/mcp-runtime/mcp-<uuid>.json)
nodes.rationale: Must hold a `mcpServers: {...}` object so the agentmemory entry can sit beside the kanbots tool-bridge entry.

nodes.label: agentmemory KV namespace scheme (mem:obs:<sessionId>, mem:team:<teamId>:shared, mem:memories, mem:graph:*)
nodes.norm_label: agentmemory kv namespace scheme (mem:obs:<sessionid>, mem:team:<teamid>:shared, mem:memories, mem:graph:*)

nodes.label: kanbots natural scopes (chat session, issue thread, agent run, workspace repo)
nodes.norm_label: kanbots natural scopes (chat session, issue thread, agent run, workspace repo)
nodes.rationale: Backed by chat_sessions, threads/messages, agent_runs, workspace_repos tables; repoId resolved in supervisor.ts on dispatch is the source of the repo key.

nodes.label: memory.scope modes: shared (default) | team | global
nodes.rationale: shared = repo-scoped only; team adds mem:team:<teamId>:shared; global disables namespacing entirely (expert-mode footgun, UI warns).

nodes.label: Team namespace mem:team:<teamId>:shared for cross-repo sharing
nodes.norm_label: team namespace mem:team:<teamid>:shared for cross-repo sharing
nodes.rationale: Opt-in via config.json memory.teamId for monorepos / microservice portfolios with shared conventions.

nodes.label: agentmemory 12 lifecycle hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, Stop, ...)
nodes.norm_label: agentmemory 12 lifecycle hooks (sessionstart, userpromptsubmit, pretooluse, posttooluse, precompact, stop, ...)

nodes.label: opts.onRunComplete callback (supervisor.ts close handler, terminal status classification)
nodes.norm_label: opts.onruncomplete callback (supervisor.ts close handler, terminal status classification)
nodes.rationale: Fires once per run with the final result including USD cost; the post-run injection point.

nodes.label: config.json `rtk.assumeInstalled` flag (presentation-only)
nodes.rationale: Lets the cost-budget UI annotate projected savings; a hint, not a measurement — kanbots cannot read RTK's own history.db analytics.

nodes.label: RTK PreToolUse hook (`rtk init -g`, rewrites `git status` -> `rtk git status`)
nodes.norm_label: rtk pretooluse hook (`rtk init -g`, rewrites `git status` -> `rtk git status`)
nodes.rationale: Transparent boundary rewrite with zero per-command context overhead; supports 16 AI tools natively, overlapping heavily with kanbots's 11.

nodes.label: RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Rust Token Killer) CLI output compressor
nodes.norm_label: rtk (rtk-ai/rtk, rust token killer) cli output compressor
nodes.rationale: Single Rust binary with 64 command filters (git, cargo, npm/pnpm, pytest, docker, kubectl, ...) that compresses verbose command output before the agent reads it, preserving exit codes and falling back to raw output on filter failure. Not an agent framework, MCP server, or memory system. Token savings are bytes/4 estimates (reliable ratios, approximate absolutes). Name collision with reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit); verify with `rtk gain`.

nodes.label: RTK PATH detection on startup (`which rtk` + `rtk --version`)
nodes.norm_label: rtk path detection on startup (`which rtk` + `rtk --version`)
nodes.rationale: Informational parity with ADR-0002's agentmemory detection: shows 'RTK: active' in Settings if present, no nag if absent; cheap, non-blocking, fails silently.

nodes.label: Agent state keys (idle/queued/running/blocked/review/failed)
nodes.rationale: Agent states map to agent:* GitHub labels in GitHub mode.

nodes.label: .kanbots/ workspace directory
nodes.rationale: Always refers to the .kanbots/ inside the opened workspace, never this repo's own; all per-run state is isolated there.

nodes.label: Board status keys (backlog/todo/inProgress/review/done)
nodes.rationale: Status keys map 1:1 to GitHub labels status:* so local mode and GitHub mode share one vocabulary.

nodes.label: Inbox column (issues with no status:* label)
nodes.norm_label: inbox column (issues with no status:* label)

nodes.label: Sentry ingestion (client -> store -> API -> poller -> UI) as the template
nodes.norm_label: sentry ingestion (client -> store -> api -> poller -> ui) as the template
nodes.rationale: Mapped end-to-end (sentry-client.ts, migration 0010, sentry-config/imports repos, handlers/sentry.ts, sentry-poller.ts, SentrySettingsModal.tsx); the vagas ingestion copies this skeleton layer by layer.

nodes.label: vagas_config table (migration 0031_vagas)
nodes.rationale: Singleton config mirroring sentry_config but simpler: no token, no encryption, no safeStorage because the site is public. 0031 is the next free migration number (0011 taken, 0019 reserved).

nodes.label: vagas_imports table (vaga_id PK -> local_issues.number, status imported|viewed|applied|dismissed)
nodes.norm_label: vagas_imports table (vaga_id pk -> local_issues.number, status imported|viewed|applied|dismissed)
nodes.rationale: De-duplication key is the numeric vaga_id from the detail URL; cascade-deletes with local_issues.

nodes.label: IPC handlers vagas:* (get-config, save-config, test-connection, sync-now, set-status)
nodes.norm_label: ipc handlers vagas:* (get-config, save-config, test-connection, sync-now, set-status)
nodes.rationale: No analyze / apply-suggestion — these are job leads, not errors to triage with Claude; setStatus replaces them. HandlerDeps gains a VagasRuntime { syncNow, restartPoller } strictly smaller than SentryRuntime.

nodes.label: VagasClient (packages/core/src/vagas-client.ts) — proposed
nodes.rationale: Mirrors SentryClient's injectable-fetch shape for testability; page-1-only listListings(); 403/503 -> VagasBlockError, other non-OK -> VagasRequestError; no auth errors because the site is public.

nodes.label: VagasListing (vagaId, title, detailUrl, company, location, salary)
nodes.norm_label: vagaslisting (vagaid, title, detailurl, company, location, salary)

nodes.label: VagasPoller (packages/desktop/src/vagas-poller.ts) — proposed
nodes.rationale: Structurally identical to sentry-poller.ts: recursive setTimeout, inFlight coalescing, 300–86400s clamp, default 1800s, MAX_LISTINGS_PER_SYNC=50. Unlike Sentry it never auto-disables on failure (no auth to fix) — exponential backoff to a ceiling and keep retrying.

nodes.label: VagasSettingsModal (packages/web) — proposed
nodes.rationale: Clone of SentrySettingsModal: enabled toggle, search URL, poll interval, UA override, sync now; imported cards appear on the normal board, no dedicated Jobs view in v1.

nodes.label: ADR template (docs/adr/template.md)
nodes.rationale: Sections kept: Status, Date, Context, Decision, Alternatives Considered, Consequences, References — only the sections that earn their keep.

nodes.label: Spec 0001 — vagas.com.br job ingestion
nodes.rationale: Status Draft, awaiting decision on §9 fetching strategy. Ingestion is interpreted as a Sentry-style external source that creates Inbox triage cards, not a generic plugin framework.

nodes.label: Lightweight ADR convention
nodes.rationale: Fork is about to make non-obvious integration choices (memory layer, cost optimization, MCP wiring, scoping) whose rationale would be expensive to reconstruct from commits. Chose a trimmed MADR/Nygard hybrid over (A) commit messages only (they omit rejected alternatives), (B) full MADR with YAML frontmatter (too much ceremony for a solo fork), (C) inline decision notes in descriptive docs (buried, unenumerable). Rules: docs/adr/, NNNN-kebab-case, never renumber, one decision per ADR, no code in ADRs.

nodes.label: Superseded three-tier model (kanbots -> agentmemory -> rtk toolkit layer)
nodes.norm_label: superseded three-tier model (kanbots -> agentmemory -> rtk toolkit layer)
nodes.rationale: Rejected because it was based on misidentifying rtk as an orchestration/toolkit layer; rtk exposes no SDK adapters or pipeline runner, so forcing it into that role would mean building the layer ourselves.

nodes.label: Two-axis integration model (memory axis + cost axis)
nodes.norm_label: two-axis integration model (memory axis + cost axis)
nodes.rationale: agentmemory and rtk are orthogonal — rtk has zero overlap with memory, orchestration, or MCP — so they are integrated as two decoupled axes rather than a layered stack. Either can be adopted or rolled back without the other. agentmemory is sequenced first (larger quality win, unblocks cross-run continuity); rtk last (small self-contained cost win). Rejected: three-tier model (misidentified rtk), agentmemory-only (drops a cheap cost win), in-house reimplementation (diverts effort from kanbots-specific work).

nodes.label: Health-gated dispatch (warn, don't fail, when memory server unreachable)
nodes.norm_label: health-gated dispatch (warn, don't fail, when memory server unreachable)
nodes.rationale: Memory is an enhancement, not a precondition for a run; unreachable server emits a warning event on agent-runs:events and dispatch proceeds.

nodes.label: Hybrid lifecycle: detect, optionally manage, never force
nodes.norm_label: hybrid lifecycle: detect, optionally manage, never force
nodes.rationale: If kanbots assumes the server is up, failure is quiet; if it force-starts, agentmemory becomes a hard dependency and collides with standalone instances on :49134. So: detect on startup, optional managed start (default off) supervised like agent runs with logs in .kanbots/logs/agentmemory.log, record versions in .kanbots/db.sqlite. Rejected: always-managed (coercive, port conflicts), external-only (quiet failure), per-workspace default (multiplies ports/engines, loses cross-workspace sharing), embed-as-library (agentmemory is a server with its own engine process).

nodes.label: Port-conflict-aware startup (never kill a standalone instance)
nodes.norm_label: port-conflict-aware startup (never kill a standalone instance)
nodes.rationale: If :49134 or :3111 is already bound, treat detection as success and log the incident; killing a user's standalone agentmemory would be the worst kind of surprise.

nodes.label: AgentCliAdapter.mcpSupport flag ('file' | 'flags' | 'config-dir' | 'none')
nodes.rationale: Keeps 'which CLIs support MCP' explicit in the adapter registry rather than scattered conditionals; 'none' routes to ADR-0005's prompt-prefix REST fallback.

nodes.label: Principle: never mutate the user's global agent config
nodes.norm_label: principle: never mutate the user's global agent config
nodes.rationale: All wiring is workspace-scoped and transient under .kanbots/; unlike `agentmemory connect`, kanbots never writes ~/.claude/settings.json or equivalents.

nodes.label: Workspace-controlled agentmemory MCP wiring via prepareForRun()
nodes.norm_label: workspace-controlled agentmemory mcp wiring via prepareforrun()
nodes.rationale: Extend the existing prepareForRun() extension point (already used for kanbots's own tool-bridge MCP) instead of relying on `agentmemory connect` writing global config: spawned agents in worktrees may bypass global config via explicit --mcp-config, and mutating ~/.claude/settings.json violates workspace isolation. Persisted toggle in config.json `memory` section; per-adapter translation (file merge for Claude Code, -c mcp_servers.* flags for Codex); REST fallback for MCP-less adapters. Rejected: SQLite MCP table (over-engineered for one server), env-vars only (necessary but not sufficient), kanbots-side MCP proxy (pointless indirection).

nodes.label: Cross-agent visibility within a scope (Claude's memory visible to Codex)
nodes.norm_label: cross-agent visibility within a scope (claude's memory visible to codex)
nodes.rationale: Namespace is keyed by workspace+repo, not by agent CLI, so knowledge inherits across the 11 CLIs by default — a stated benefit of the integration. Per-agent isolation is an advanced toggle.

nodes.label: Opt-in hard isolation via per-workspace agentmemory instance (--data-dir .kanbots/agentmemory-data/)
nodes.norm_label: opt-in hard isolation via per-workspace agentmemory instance (--data-dir .kanbots/agentmemory-data/)
nodes.rationale: Heaviest option (separate process, ports, engine); documented as 'only when legal or hygienic isolation demands it', e.g. client work that must never share memory with personal projects.

nodes.label: Repo-scoped session namespace kanbots:<workspaceId>:<repoId>:<issueNumber>:<runId>
nodes.rationale: agentmemory has no native per-repo isolation, so per-repo recall is implemented on top of its session-ID mechanism: recall is prefixed with kanbots:<workspaceId>:<repoId>, giving repo A's runs continuity across issues/agents/time without seeing repo B. Rejected: per-repo daemon (multiplies ports/engines, :49134 conflict), global namespace (cross-contamination), kanbots-side filtering shim (duplicates agentmemory scoping, adds latency), per-agent isolation by default (breaks cross-agent continuity). Risk: encoding is a kanbots convention layered on agentmemory; keep it in one place and pin the version.

nodes.label: Agent-driven checkpoint via agentmemory hooks (SessionStart/PostToolUse/Stop) + memory_save tools
nodes.norm_label: agent-driven checkpoint via agentmemory hooks (sessionstart/posttooluse/stop) + memory_save tools
nodes.rationale: Primary checkpoint path with zero kanbots code beyond wiring; the Stop hook writes the session summary, memory_save / memory_lessons_save capture deliberate 'I decided X because Y' entries.

nodes.label: Cost-aware recall trimming (K=3 -> K=1 -> one-line hint)
nodes.norm_label: cost-aware recall trimming (k=3 -> k=1 -> one-line hint)
nodes.rationale: Recall tokens count against runCostBudgetUsd; when budget is tight kanbots trims K rather than skipping, and a run with zero budget skips the block but keeps MCP wired.

nodes.label: Decision-event capture (resolved decision question/answer written to memory)
nodes.norm_label: decision-event capture (resolved decision question/answer written to memory)
nodes.rationale: kanbots is the only actor that sees the human-resolved decision, so this is the one piece of kanbots-native memory content; high-value, human-validated.

nodes.label: kanbots fallback checkpoint in onRunComplete (only when nothing was written)
nodes.norm_label: kanbots fallback checkpoint in onruncomplete (only when nothing was written)
nodes.rationale: Checks memory_sessions for the run's session ID; if empty and status is complete, writes a minimal entry (issue title, status, cost, branch/worktree, issue URL) without attempting to summarize — a missing summary means hooks didn't fire, not that kanbots should improvise. Avoids coupling to adapter event schemas.

nodes.label: Hybrid injection/checkpoint: kanbots nudges + injects recall; agent writes checkpoint; kanbots fallback only if agent didn't
nodes.norm_label: hybrid injection/checkpoint: kanbots nudges + injects recall; agent writes checkpoint; kanbots fallback only if agent didn't
nodes.rationale: Wiring MCP makes memory reachable but not used. Pure passive risks no recall from weaker models; pure active forces kanbots to parse 11 adapters' event schemas and duplicates agentmemory's consolidation. Hybrid: guaranteed compact recall in the prompt prefix, agent-driven checkpoint via agentmemory hooks/MCP, minimal kanbots fallback when nothing was written. Rejected: hooks-only (hook support varies across agents), full recall in every prompt (blows cost budget, loses on-demand querying).

nodes.label: Pre-run compact recall block in the prompt prefix (top-K smart-search, K=3)
nodes.norm_label: pre-run compact recall block in the prompt prefix (top-k smart-search, k=3)
nodes.rationale: Calls POST /agentmemory/smart-search with issue title+body scoped per ADR-0004, prepends a token-capped 'Relevant project memory' block to appendSystemPrompt in composeSystemPrompt(); ends by advertising memory_recall/memory_smart_search MCP tools. Guarantees every run starts with context even if the agent never calls MCP. Sub-second timeout, degrade gracefully (skip block) consistent with ADR-0002's health-gated dispatch.

nodes.label: Document-only RTK integration for v1 (user installs globally; no kanbots code)
nodes.norm_label: document-only rtk integration for v1 (user installs globally; no kanbots code)
nodes.rationale: RTK's PreToolUse hook lives in the user's global agent config and is already active for kanbots-spawned agents once `rtk init -g` has run, so kanbots adds a docs page (docs/rtk.md), PATH detection, and an optional assumeInstalled flag — nothing more. Rejected: auto-install + per-agent rtk init (fights RTK's global design, forces binary download, silent rewriting is hard to debug), wrapping commands at the spawn layer (kanbots doesn't see the agent's internal Bash calls), per-worktree settings.json (redundant unless disabling is needed), not documenting at all (real cost win for exactly this workload). Downside: benefit only realized by users who read the docs; compression can mask signals the agent needed.

nodes.label: Compliance policy: honest User-Agent, robots-respecting path scope, rate limits, public metadata only
nodes.norm_label: compliance policy: honest user-agent, robots-respecting path scope, rate limits, public metadata only
nodes.rationale: vagas.com.br is behind Cloudflare with robots.txt blocking AI crawlers but not /vagas-de-tecnologia; no official API/RSS exists; ToS targets CV/recruiter data, not public listings. So: no UA spoofing, never hit /api/, /v1/, /auth/, /users/, /token/, /vagas/pesquisas, one request per sync, exponential backoff on blocks, and a legal-review gate before non-personal use.

nodes.label: Decision A — fetching strategy (A1 fetch+cheerio page-1 recommended; A2 hidden BrowserWindow; A3 Playwright)
nodes.norm_label: decision a — fetching strategy (a1 fetch+cheerio page-1 recommended; a2 hidden browserwindow; a3 playwright)
nodes.rationale: A1 recommended for v1: mirrors SentryClient, no heavy deps, dedup makes page-1 viable. A2 couples client to desktop and is hard to unit-test; A3 is a heavy dep redundant in an Electron app. listListings() is written so A2/A3 can slot in later without touching poller/store/UI.

nodes.label: Decision B — cheerio in @kanbots/core vs. parse helper in desktop
nodes.norm_label: decision b — cheerio in @kanbots/core vs. parse helper in desktop
nodes.rationale: Recommend cheerio in core for consistency with where domain clients live; revisit if core must stay parser-free like SentryClient.

nodes.label: Decision C — job postings as ordinary Inbox triage cards, not a Jobs board view
nodes.norm_label: decision c — job postings as ordinary inbox triage cards, not a jobs board view
nodes.rationale: Matches the Sentry precedent and needs the least code.

nodes.label: Stable key: numeric {id} from /vagas/{id}/{slug}, not CSS classes
nodes.norm_label: stable key: numeric {id} from /vagas/{id}/{slug}, not css classes
nodes.rationale: Selectors have churned historically (li.vaga -> article), so identity must come from the URL path; parser falls back across selector strategies.
